measurement: live portrait Phase 1: the service runtime (services/portrait) on the GPU (scripts/portrait_runtime_check.py)
environment: spike venv over rpg-stt (CPython 3.11, torch 2.6.0+cu124); models installed through the catalog's direct and Hugging Face paths into resources/models/portrait; GPU otherwise idle
inputs: portrait: upstream sam_altman_512x512.jpg (and sam_altman.webp for the crop); audio: aud-sample-vs-1, Maya, Morgan, Sofia fed one video frame at a time as 16-bit PCM; nfe 7, R 5, H 20, decode batch 4
findings: With float input and no buffer padding the service's motion latents equal the spike's exactly (0.0); 16-bit PCM moves them 2%.

Each new wav2vec2 input length costs about 0.4 s and each new decoder batch size about 28 s of one-off GPU setup; the service feeds both one fixed shape (100-frame buffer with silence before it, decode batches of exactly 4) and warms them at load.

torchvision's GPU JPEG encoder returned noise for some frames (PSNR 18 dB on average against the decoded frames), which SyncNet scored as lost sync (LSE-C 4.4); the service encodes on the CPU (every sent frame within 43 dB of its decoded frame).
Open: load takes about 60 s (mostly decoder setup), and the first pass of an output after a few idle seconds took 80-350 ms instead of 24 ms.
